overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of what a neural network is made of and how training changes it. You'll be asked about neurons, weights, and layers, about parameters, about prediction error and loss, and about gradient descent and backpropagation.

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

forms.stemHtml: What does a single artificial neuron do?

options.html: It stores one fact from the training data so the network can look it up
options.text: It stores one fact from the training data so the network can look it up
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. A neuron stores no facts. It weighs the numbers it receives and passes one number on.

options.html: It compares the network's prediction with the right answer
options.text: It compares the network's prediction with the right answer
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Comparing predictions with right answers is part of training and isn't done by a neuron. A neuron weighs the numbers it receives and passes one number on.

options.html: It weighs the numbers it receives and passes one number on
options.text: It weighs the numbers it receives and passes one number on
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Each neuron multiplies its incoming numbers by their weights, combines the results, and sends a single number forward to the next layer.

options.html: It decides which layer of the network should handle each input
options.text: It decides which layer of the network should handle each input
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Numbers pass through every layer in order, and no neuron routes them. A neuron weighs the numbers it receives and passes one number on.

forms.stemHtml: Two networks have exactly the same design: the same layers, the same neurons, and the same connections. One identifies animals in photographs, and the other tells indoor scenes from outdoor ones. What makes them behave differently?

options.html: Their engineers wrote a different set of rules into each network
options.text: Their engineers wrote a different set of rules into each network
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Nobody writes rules into a neural network. The two networks differ in their parameter values, which training set differently for each.

options.html: Their parameters were set to different values by training
options.text: Their parameters were set to different values by training
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A design does nothing in particular on its own. The same network with different parameter settings does a different job.

options.html: Their layers pass numbers forward in a different order
options.text: Their layers pass numbers forward in a different order
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The networks have the same design, so numbers move through them in the same order. They differ in their parameter values.

options.html: Their neurons each hold a different stored photograph
options.text: Their neurons each hold a different stored photograph
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Networks don't store their training examples. The two networks differ in their parameter values, which training set differently for each.

options.html: A single score for how wrong a model's predictions are
options.text: A single score for how wrong a model's predictions are
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The loss combines the prediction errors over many examples into one number, and training works to bring that number down.

options.html: The share of training examples a model fails to store
options.text: The share of training examples a model fails to store
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. A model doesn't store its training examples at all. The loss is a single score for how wrong a model's predictions are, averaged over many examples.

options.html: The number of parameters a model sheds during training
options.text: The number of parameters a model sheds during training
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Training adjusts parameters and doesn't remove them. The loss is a single score for how wrong a model's predictions are, averaged over many examples.

options.html: The amount of data left out of a model's training set
options.text: The amount of data left out of a model's training set
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Loss has nothing to do with missing data. It's a single score for how wrong a model's predictions are, averaged over many examples.

forms.stemHtml: During a training step, what does backpropagation contribute?

options.html: It picks the examples the network will be trained on
options.text: It picks the examples the network will be trained on
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The builders choose the training data. Backpropagation works backward through the network and gives each parameter its share of the responsibility for the error.

options.html: It sets every parameter to a random starting value
options.text: It sets every parameter to a random starting value
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. That's random initialization, which happens once before training. Backpropagation works backward through the network and gives each parameter its share of the responsibility for the error.

options.html: It tells the network in plain words which patterns it should look for
options.text: It tells the network in plain words which patterns it should look for
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Nobody tells a network what patterns to find. Backpropagation works backward through the network and gives each parameter its share of the responsibility for the error.

options.html: It gives each parameter its share of the blame for the error
options.text: It gives each parameter its share of the blame for the error
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Backpropagation works backward from the output and finds, for every parameter, which way and how much to adjust it.

forms.stemHtml: Which of these statements about training by gradient descent are accurate? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: The parameters start at random values
options.text: The parameters start at random values
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A network's parameters are set at random before training, and training then adjusts them.

options.html: Each step changes the parameters only slightly
options.text: Each step changes the parameters only slightly
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The learning rate keeps each adjustment small, so the effects of many examples can add up.

options.html: Each training example is saved inside the network
options.text: Each training example is saved inside the network
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Examples aren't stored. What remains is their combined effect on the parameter values.

options.html: The steps move toward a lower loss
options.text: The steps move toward a lower loss
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Each step nudges the parameters in the direction that lowers the loss.

options.html: Engineers set the final value of each weight by hand
options.text: Engineers set the final value of each weight by hand
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Training sets the weights. Engineers choose the design, the data, the objective, and the learning rate.

title: Neural networks and how training adjusts them
